content.title: Who's Watching the Artemis II Launch? - Other - Chief Delphi
content.text: post by sgeckler on Apr 1 The Artemis II launch is scheduled for 6:24pm EDT today. This will be during our team meeting so that means NASA LIVE will be on in our shop! How cool! I was 3 years old the last time a person when around the moon! - yeah I know don’t tell me how old I am :). post by Astro1 on Apr 1 Yes! I’m incredibly excited. The technological and scientific progress this could trigger is amazing, and I’m so glad a new generation will be able to witness this. post by arshonb on Apr 1 I’m sure they had a good reason for this… post by BSV on Apr 1 Watching from the space center causeway and then trying to catch an early flight back to our regional tomorrow if it launches - otherwise I’ll hang out for a couple more days and hope for at least one more attempt (the team is in good hands so I am not in a rush). One of my kids is a FIRST alumni working the launch - it’s amazing to see what they do after they graduate from FIRST. post by rwwin on Apr 1 We have a mentor with Lockheed Martin that put in about 15 years between the original CEV project and carried through with Orion until 2020 and will be heading in to one of the office launch parties. post by Imagery_Lead on Apr 1 Outside of the live stream, they also have a cool hype trailer for the launch! There is also a livestream by NASA Spaceflight (not NASA) who does commentary and does a lot of aerospace talk. They discuss a lot of stuff going on and how past tests went compared to current events (ex: how wet dress before had some leaks, but currently have not seen many issues). post by Dave_Ebersol on Apr 1 I’ve been CTE Director of my District for only 2 weeks now. Below is my first all Staff, Students, and Family email. On a personal note, I am running my families Seder for Passover tonight, and have timed our first cup of “grape juice” to coincide with the launch. Subject: TO THE MOON!!!: Artemis II Launch Set for Wednesday 4/1 at 6:24 pm Hello, I just wanted to invite you all to watch the Artemis 2 mission launch. The launch set for tomorrow Wednesday April 1st at 6:24 pm. This launch will be our next step in landing back on the moon in over 50 years!!! This mission will also have the first woman to set foot on moon. This 10-day, four-astronaut mission will launch from Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39B. This will be the first crewed flight around the Moon since 1972, testing the Orion capsule and SLS rocket. Artemis is a 3-part mission Artemis 1 = Launched the morning of Monday 11/16/22 and was an unmanned 40-day space mission used to gather important flight and scientific data for the manned missions. Artemis 2 = Launching April of 2026, will be the first manned mission to orbit the moon in more than 50 years. Artemis 3 = Launching Winter of 2027 will be the first manned mission to have astronauts step foot on the moon in more than 50 years.
